title: Design JMAP Pile extension: multi-membership file groups (was: bags)
description:
Idea (Mark, 2026-11-02): a generic JMAP extension (not chat-specific) for "bags of files" as an alternative to folder trees (FileNode/WebDAV). Bags and files carry tags; a file may be in more than one bag; bags and files have classification, access control, and/or capacity. A Space could be one bag; SpaceFile (jmap-chat-spec-7snc) stays flat.

Working design (proposed, not decided):
- Access: UNION over bags (any bag granting access grants it), made safe by a classification gate on membership: each file has a classification, each bag a classification ceiling; a file may only join bags whose ceiling >= its classification (Bell-LaPadula no-write-down; cf. Purview sensitivity labels).
- Rejected access rules: plain union (adding to an open bag silently publishes); intersection (adding to a tight bag silently hides elsewhere); Drive-style home bag + shortcuts (rebuilds single-parent).
- Capacity: per-bag limit = sum of member sizes; a file counts against every bag it is in; bytes stored once per account. No owning bag.
- Tags: free-form, no access semantics, for query only (same as 7snc Q7 labels).

Open questions:
1. Can bags contain bags? Leaning no (nesting reintroduces trees + ACL inheritance).
2. File removed from its last bag: destroy, or keep as orphan?
3. Per-file ACL in addition to bag ACL? Two systems to reconcile; leaning no.
4. Classification model: ordered levels only, or levels + compartments? Who may reclassify; what happens to existing memberships when a file is upclassified above a bag's ceiling.
5. Relationship to FileNode and SpaceFile: replace, coexist, or mirror.
6. Federation.

Prior art (from memory, unverified): Perkeep sets (multi-membership, sharing a set shares members = union); CMIS multi-filing (ACL on object, folders grant nothing); Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels on documents and containers (mismatch is audited, not blocked); Google Photos / Flickr albums / Are.na channels (union, known leaks); Placeless Documents (Xerox PARC ~1999); Gifford Semantic File System (1991), TMSU/Tagsistant; Trusted Solaris / SELinux MLS; S3 tags in IAM (tags DO grant access; hard to audit). Apparent gap: nobody combines multi-membership + per-bag ACL + classification gate + capacity in one sync-friendly API. Verify with a research pass before drafting (esp. Are.na permissions, whether Purview can block mismatches).

Keyword discipline: per bcp14-keyword-discipline memory, access-control requirements are SHOULD.
notes:
Working name (Mark, 2026-11-02): Pile. Precedent: Apple 'Piles' research (Mander, Salomon, Wong, CHI 1992), informal grouping of documents without folders. Avoids taken names: Set (JMAP /set), Collection (WebDAV RFC 4918), Folder/Directory (tree), Mailbox (JMAP Mail), Bag (BagIt RFC 8493; multiset), Bucket (S3 single-membership), Crate (Rust, RO-Crate). Other candidates considered: Board, Album, Playlist. Type would be Pile with Pile/get,/changes,/set,/query,/queryChanges.
Constraint (Mark, 2026-11-02): a Pile groups existing objects (SpaceFile, FileNode, blobs); Piles never define a file object of their own. Name/type/size live on the grouped object. Reason: avoid three overlapping file layers in a Space; SpaceFile (7snc) is the flat file object for core chat, FileNode the optional tree. If every Space later becomes a Pile, SpaceFile.spaceId becomes one kind of Pile membership. Also note leave-to-implementations memory: decide first whether Piles define access control at all.
